title: Senior Computer Vision & AI Engineer
description:
Do you want to build computer-vision technology that helps autonomous drones understand and navigate the real world?

At Robotto, we build advanced autonomy and software solutions for drones and unmanned systems. Our work brings together computer vision, edge computing, software, electronics and real-world product development.We are looking for a Senior Computer Vision & AI Engineer to take a leading technical role in developing and improving the perception capabilities behind our drone platform.You will work on challenging real-world problems where robust vision, accurate localisation and reliable performance matter. This is an opportunity for someone who enjoys going beyond algorithms and prototypes to build computer-vision solutions that perform reliably in demanding real-world environments.

The role
You will join a highly technical engineering team working on autonomy for drones and unmanned systems.You will take significant ownership of computer-vision capabilities supporting object detection, tracking, visual localisation, visual-inertial odometry and other perception-related challenges.You will work closely with software, control, flight-test and electronics colleagues to turn computer-vision concepts into robust, deployable solutions.As a senior engineer, you will also contribute to architecture and technical decisions, help strengthen engineering practices and share your experience with other engineers across the team.

What you will do
  • Design, develop, test and improve advanced computer-vision algorithms for Robotto’s drone and autonomy platform.
  • Take technical ownership of computer-vision problems from exploration and prototyping through implementation, evaluation and deployment.
  • Work with object detection, tracking, visual localisation, visual-inertial odometry, visual SLAM and related perception challenges.
  • Build robust solutions that can perform under changing environmental and operational conditions.
  • Optimise computer-vision solutions for deployment on edge and resource-constrained computing platforms.
  • Define appropriate datasets, test scenarios, evaluation methods and performance metrics.
  • Contribute to architecture and technical-design decisions across the perception stack.
  • Collaborate closely with software, control, flight-test and electronics engineers to integrate perception capabilities into the wider platform.
  • Investigate complex technical issues, validate results and drive practical improvements.
  • Contribute to code quality, testing, documentation and engineering practices.
  • Share knowledge and provide technical guidance to other engineers where relevant.

What success could look like in your first 3–6 months
  • You have developed a strong understanding of Robotto’s autonomy platform, architecture and computer-vision priorities.
  • You have taken ownership of one or more important perception challenges and are driving them towards robust solutions.
  • You have contributed meaningful improvements to areas such as object detection, tracking, localisation or visual-inertial odometry.
  • Your solutions are being evaluated against real-world data and operational scenarios.
  • You are contributing to architecture and technical decisions across the computer-vision stack.
  • You are collaborating effectively across computer vision, software, control and flight testing.
  • You have become a trusted senior technical contributor within the engineering team.

What we are looking for
We are looking for an experienced engineer with a strong computer-vision foundation and a track record of turning complex technical ideas into practical, working systems.
  • 5+ years of relevant professional experience preferred, with significant hands-on expertise in computer vision, robotics, machine learning, autonomy or a closely related field.
  • Strong practical knowledge of computer vision, with experience in areas such as object detection, tracking, visual localisation, visual-inertial odometry, visual SLAM or related perception methods.
  • Strong C++ programming skills, with Python experience for algorithm development, experimentation, testing and prototyping.
  • Experience taking computer-vision or machine-learning solutions beyond research and prototyping into real products or deployed systems.
  • Experience designing, training and evaluating deep-learning models for computer-vision applications.
  • Experience deploying and optimising models or computer-vision algorithms on edge or resource-constrained computing platforms is highly relevant.
  • Strong understanding of algorithm evaluation, datasets, testing methodologies and measurable performance criteria.
  • Experience contributing to architecture or technical-design decisions within complex software or perception systems.
  • A good understanding of how vision systems interact with cameras, sensors, software, compute platforms and real-world environments.
  • Experience with drones, robotics, autonomous systems or embedded-adjacent software is a strong advantage.
  • Experience mentoring, supporting or sharing technical knowledge with other engineers is an advantage.
  • Professional fluency in English.
  • A degree in computer vision, robotics, computer science, engineering or a related technical field is preferred; equivalent industry or research experience is equally welcome.

Who you are
You are technically curious, analytical and comfortable taking ownership when the answer is not immediately obvious.You enjoy going deep into difficult technical problems, while keeping sight of the goal: building technology that works reliably in the real world.
  • You take ownership of technical problems and drive them towards practical solutions.
  • You are comfortable making technical decisions and explaining the trade-offs behind them.
  • You challenge assumptions constructively and are willing to explore new approaches.
  • You care about robustness, testing and measurable performance.
  • You collaborate naturally across computer vision, software, control, electronics and flight testing.
  • You enjoy sharing knowledge and helping others solve difficult technical problems.
  • You are comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where priorities evolve as the company and technology develop.

Minds and makers forging ahead together.
At Robotto, we value people who do. People who take ownership, are willing to try new things just to see if they work, and are comfortable asking for forgiveness rather than permission.We want people who are curious, proactive and excited about turning ambitious ideas into technology that works in the real world.

Our hiring process
Our process is designed to be straightforward, practical and conversational:

1. Introductory conversation with our Talent Acquisition & Recruitment Partner
A chance to learn more about Robotto, the role and what you are looking for, while giving us an opportunity to understand your background, experience and motivation.

2. Meeting with the Hiring Manager / Principal Engineer
A deeper conversation about your technical background, computer-vision experience, the systems and products you have worked on, and your approach to solving complex perception problems.

3. In-depth Technical Evaluation & Meeting with our COO
A hands-on technical session where you will receive a short assignment to prepare in advance and then work through it together with members of our technical team.The exercise will be based on a computer-vision problem relevant to the role. We are interested in how you structure the problem, reason about algorithms and architecture, evaluate trade-offs and collaborate with other engineers rather than looking for one specific answer.Following the technical evaluation, you will meet with our COO for a conversation about the role, Robotto and mutual fit.

4. Offer
If there is a strong mutual fit, we will move forward with an offer.

Why join Robotto?
Robotto is building advanced autonomy technology for drones and unmanned systems, working at the intersection of software, hardware, computer vision and real-world operations.You will join a highly technical and ambitious team at an exciting point in the company’s journey. As we continue to scale our engineering team and work on challenging new projects, you will have a meaningful opportunity to influence both our technology and how we build it.This is not a role where everything is already defined. You will have room to challenge approaches, shape technical decisions and take ownership of important parts of our computer-vision stack.Most importantly, your work will move beyond experimentation. You will see the technology integrated, tested and used on real systems in demanding environments.

Equal Employment Opportunity
Robotto is committed to providing equal employment opportunities and fostering an inclusive workplace. We recruit based on skills, experience and potential.Due to the nature of our work, certain positions may be subject to security-clearance or other eligibility requirements in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

title: Assistant Professor in High Frequency Switch-Mode Power Supplies
description:
The Digital and High-Frequency Electronics (DHFE) section at the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering, based at the university campus in Odense, seeks outstanding individuals for full-time Assistant Professor positions in Power Electronics, focusing on power management for electronic and computing devices and systems. Successful applicants are expected to contribute to the development of academic programs and the research community. Applicants should have a PhD in Power Electronics or a closely related field. 

The DHFE section focuses on conducting research in digital and high-frequency electronics, embedded systems, control, and communication, utilizing cutting-edge reconfigurable computing and sensors. The aim is to develop next-generation electronics and computing solutions that solve technology-related challenges in fields such as autonomous robots, drones, IoT, smart grid, and healthcare.

Applicants are expected to establish and maintain a research program in high-frequency power electronics and power management for computation, along with low-voltage electronic systems. The position emphasizes converter and power-management for computing platforms and resource-constrained applications, including battery-operated, energy-harvesting, mobile, autonomous, embedded, and sensor-based systems.

The section is a vital component of our Bachelor of Engineering, Bachelor of Science, and Master of Science programs in Electrical and Electronics Engineering in Odense. Currently, the section focuses on three research fields: 1) Drones for Infrastructure Inspections and Interactions, 2) High-Frequency SMPS and power management for low-power electronic systems, and 3) Telecommunication Systems. The section has 15 academics, including professors, postdoctoral fellows, PhD students, and engineers, to support research, industrial collaboration, and educational activities, and is growing steadily.

The SDU campus in Odense contains six faculties and soon a large university hospital, creating a great concentration of academics and students facilitating interdisciplinary research and rich student life. The city of Odense is culturally rich, surrounded by a vibrant and growing robotics community, and highly livable with a green-banked meandering river cutting through the centre and attractive residential areas.

 

Job Description

The position focuses on power management for resource-constrained autonomous, mobile, and embedded electronic systems. Relevant research areas include high-frequency power conversion, battery-operated systems, energy harvesting, power management architectures, embedded control, and analog/digital control of converters. The application domain spans from ultra-low-power electronics and sensors to mobile platforms, robotics, drones, IoT devices, and power management for embedded, compact, and high-performance computing systems.

The role strengthens DHFE’s research profile at the interface between power electronics, microelectronics, embedded systems, and intelligent electronic devices. It is expected to support shared research themes across SDU, including energy-efficient electronics, autonomous systems, battery-powered platforms, sensor networks, health technology, and miniaturized or distributed devices.

The successful candidate should work constructively both with colleagues within DHFE and also with colleagues from other research units, such as SDU Microelectronics, SDU Centre for Industrial Electronics, the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute, Faculty of Health (specifically Health Tech), Mechanical Engineering, and other relevant environments, translating power electronics competence into system-level contributions for electronic devices and platforms.

 

Duties

As a faculty member, you will be responsible for developing and delivering undergraduate and graduate teaching in Electronic and Electrical Engineering, with particular attention to strengthening control and power electronics within the BSc portfolio. This includes supervising students at Bachelor and Master’s level, mentoring students, integrating with the student body, and participating in education and outreach activities. Research duties include establishing an externally funded research agenda, publishing in leading journals and conferences, supervising early-career researchers, and contributing to the development of DHFE’s research environment. The candidate is also expected to contribute to external collaboration and perform service at the section, department, university, and professional levels.

 

Qualifications Required

  • The applicant should hold a doctoral degree (PhD) in Power Electronics, Electronics, or a related subject area. 

  • Demonstrated potential for teaching undergraduate and graduate courses at the university level. 

  • The applicant must have relevant research expertise in areas related to efficient and high-frequency power converters, converter control, and power management for computing or embedded electronic systems.

  • The applicant must have teaching skills that align with the content and responsibilities of the position. This includes possessing both pedagogical and professional skills essential for carrying out the tasks associated with the role. 

  • A strong track record for research fundraising is required. 

 

For further information about the position, please contact Associate Professor Tim McRae (mcrae@sdu.dk)  or the Head of the Digital and High-frequency Electronics Section, Professor Emad Samuel Malki Ebeid, e-mail: esme@sdu.dk.  

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

  • Assessment of candidates is based on the application material, and the application must be in English and include:

  • A motivation letter that clearly explains the applicant's interest, qualifications, and motivation for the position (max. 2 pages). 

  • Detailed Curriculum Vitae, including personal contact information, describing the research, along with any other relevant information, e.g. teaching experience, computational skills, etc.

  • A research plan with a focus on the development of your research line and research team. 

  • List of funded projects. 

  • Teaching Portfolio documenting teaching, learning, and supervision qualifications and approach. Any format is acceptable; see the Faculty's teaching portfolio page for inspiration.

  • Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation).

  • List of publications with the most relevant publications highlighted. 

  • Publications most relevant to the position.

  • Up to three names and emails of researchers can provide an informed reference letter at short notice. (Reference letters and other relevant qualifications may also be included.) 

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected.

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file).

 

The application deadline is November 1, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST)

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

  

Employment terms

Appointment as an assistant professor is temporary and for an initial 3-year period, and the preferred start date is from January 1, 2027. The final start date will be agreed with the successful applicant.

During employment, the assistant professor will complete the Lecturer Training Programme. 

Employment as an assistant professor requires academic qualifications at a minimum of PhD level at the time of employment. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for assistant professor as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation.

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

-

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Further information for international applicants about entering and working in Denmark. You may also visit WorkinDenmark for additional information.

title: Declaration of interest regarding PhD project in renal calcium transport
description:
Declaration of interest regarding PhD project in renal calcium transport

 

The laboratory of Henrik Dimke, Cardiovascular and Renal Research Unit at the Department of Molecular Medicine, University of Southern Denmark is seeking a highly motivated PhD student in the field of renal transport physiology. Particular emphasis will be placed on signalling through the calcium-sensing receptor and the regulation of renal calcium transport in transgenic models.

 

Research environment

The PhD student will join the laboratory of Professor Henrik Dimke in the Cardiovascular and Renal Research Unit. The laboratory studies epithelial ion transport and the mechanisms that maintain calcium, magnesium, and phosphate balance, with particular emphasis on renal calcium transport, the calcium-sensing receptor, claudins, and kidney stone disease. The Research Unit focuses on innovative molecular and biomedical research related to cardiovascular and renal physiology. We offer a stimulating, international research environment where English is the preferred language at meetings and seminars. You will work in the modern NytSUND building, which is directly connected to the new Odense University Hospital and provides state-of-the-art laboratory and animal facilities. You can read more about the department and institute here.

 

Project description

The project will investigate how altered calcium-sensing receptor (CASR) signalling disrupts the endocrine and renal control of calcium homeostasis. Particular attention will be given to autosomal dominant hypocalcaemia type 1, in which excessive CASR activity suppresses parathyroid hormone secretion and promotes renal calcium loss. The project will examine the signalling mechanisms linking CASR activation to renal calcium transport and whole-body calcium balance. The successful applicant will use clinically relevant genetic models, including inducible and cell-specific transgenic approaches, together with detailed physiological characterization, molecular and biochemical techniques, and imaging.

 

Qualifications

Qualified and highly motivated candidates from all nationalities are encouraged to apply. 

 

The successful applicant must have

  • A Master's degree (Danish: kandidatgrad) or another relevant degree that concludes a research-based study programme of minimum five years’ duration at an institution of higher education. If you do not have a Master's degree, the Graduate School will make an individual assessment of your academic qualifications.

  • Good oral and written English language skills

  • you must at the time of submission have documented research experience. E.g. be the author or co-author of an article in a peer-reviewed international journal (must at least be submitted) or of a published abstract from an international scientific conference, or have worked as research assistant full time for at least 6 months (after completing your masters degree). The research experience of each applicant is individually assessed by the Graduate School.

 

The successful applicant should have

  • The ability to work independently and in a structured manner. 

  • Good collaborative and interpersonal skills. 

  • Previous experience with experimental animal work or relevant molecular and biochemical techniques, such as western blotting or immunohistochemistry, is preferred but not required.

 

For further information about the project, please contact:

Professor Henrik Dimke

Department of Molecular Medicine

University of Southern Denmark (SDU)

Tel. +45 65 50 83 10 E-mail: hdimke@health.sdu.dk


Applications must include:

• A letter stating the interest, motivation and qualifications for the project (max. 2 pages) - upload under “Application form”.
• Detailed CV, including personal contact information
• Certified copy of diploma (Master’s degree in a relevant field)

• • Contact details for at least one professional reference who may be contacted during the assessment process.


Shortlisting may be used in the assessment process. References will normally be contacted only for shortlisted candidates.

Further information about the PhD-program can be found at the homepage of the University.


Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now". Attached files must be in Adobe PDF format. We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.

Incomplete applications and applications received after the deadline will neither be considered nor evaluated. 

 

Closing date: October 12th, 2026


Successful candidates will be asked to send an application to the PhD Secretariat, Faculty of Health Sciences, to be enrolled as PhD students.

 

The PhD programme will be carried out in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order).

 

Salary and Working Conditions at SDU

PhD students employed at SDU are employed as PhD fellows according to the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations in public employment (AC) agreement.


Salary and any salary supplement are paid according to your seniority level and as negotiated with your union representative. The base salary (excluding 18.07% pension contribution) is DKK 374,912.98.

 

The Faculty of Health Sciences at the University of Southern Denmark is one of Denmark’s leading faculties of health sciences. With nine departments, internationally top‑class research, and a broad range of health‑related study programmes, we contribute to developing the knowledge, treatments, and healthcare system of the future.

 

As an employee at the faculty, you become part of an ambitious and interdisciplinary environment characterised by high academic standards, strong collaborations, and excellent opportunities for professional development. The faculty has activities in Odense, Esbjerg, and Copenhagen. In Esbjerg and Copenhagen, strong academic communities provide the framework for research and education, while our modern faculty building in Odense brings research, education, and administration together under one roof and is directly connected to Odense University Hospital.

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

title: PhD Position(s) in Bioreceptive Design and Robotic 3D Printing for Living System Integration in Architecture
description:
SDU CREATE invites highly motivated candidates who wish to contribute to a regenerative built environment to apply for one or more PhD positions in Computational Design and Fabrication for Living System Integration in Architecture. The position(s) is expected to begin in January 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The application deadline is 15 October 2026 at 23:59 CEST.

Scope of the work

The PhD position(s) is linked to the Villum CEBE programme, Civil Engineering and the Green Transition in the Built Environment, funded by the Villum Foundation. Within Research Field 2, Design for Regeneration, Circularity and Longevity, the research will develop architectural interfaces that support the establishment and growth of living systems, particularly photosynthetic communities, as a strategy for regenerative architecture. The focus is on enveloping surfaces in the built environment.

The project will focus on designing, testing and demonstrating, at architectural scale, porous mineral interfaces combined with hydrogels. Computational design, fabrication and environmental monitoring will be combined with cultivation experiments and biological assessment, targeting mosses, algae and cyanobacteria in collaboration with partner researchers in biology.

We seek candidates with primary expertise in one of two complementary research profiles:

  • Bioreceptive Design and Robotic 3D Printing: exploring how architectural geometry, material composition and 3D printing can create bioreceptive interfaces. The work will combine computational design, printable material development, toolpath generation and robot programming to develop porous mineral interfaces informed by biological requirements.

  • Living Material Design and Biological Performance: developing hydrogels incorporating living organisms for integration into porous mineral interfaces. The work will combine formulation, cultivation, sensors, automated monitoring and data analysis to evaluate hygrothermal behaviour, biological growth, photosynthetic activity and material performance.

Both profiles require an interest in integrating biological systems and processes into architectural design and construction. The successful candidate(s) will collaborate within the team to develop and validate the resulting interfaces.

The candidate(s) will also contribute to the Centre’s activities, including teaching in the MSc CREATE programme and the BSc programme in Civil and Architectural Engineering through teaching, workshops and co-supervision of student projects.

Focus Area and Research Project

The research will investigate how material composition, porous morphologies and hygrothermal dynamics can support biological establishment and environmental performance, while addressing durability, maintenance and integration into building envelopes. Environmental measurements will help establish relationships between interface design, climatic exposure, biological development and performance.

The successful candidate(s) will contribute to selected areas according to their expertise, working within a team with complementary skills:

  • Computational design of bioreceptive mineral interfaces for enveloping surfaces in the built environment

  • Development and characterisation of printable mineral materials

  • Robotic 3D printing, toolpath generation and fabrication process development

  • Formulation of hydrogels incorporating living organisms and their integration into printed scaffolds

  • Cultivation experiments and assessment of biological growth and photosynthetic activity

  • Sensor integration, automated monitoring and data analysis to evaluate hygrothermal behaviour, ecological and microclimatic performance

  • Fabrication and evaluation of full-scale architectural demonstrators, addressing durability, maintenance and sustained biological growth

About SDU CREATE’s Research Environment

The Centre for Computational Research in Emergent Architectural Technology and Engineering, SDU CREATE, is led by Associate Professor Roberto Naboni. The Centre investigates advanced concepts and applications in architectural engineering, focusing on computational design, construction robotics, and material innovation. SDU CREATE brings together an international research team working across architectural engineering, computer science, robotics, materials science, and biology. Its research develops sustainable, regenerative approaches to designing and constructing the built environment.

Located within the Faculty of Engineering at the University of Southern Denmark, SDU CREATE provides advanced laboratory facilities for robotic fabrication, additive and subtractive manufacturing, mixed reality applications in design and construction, and structural and mechanical testing. The facilities include industrial robotic systems, computational design platforms, and equipment for the experimental testing of materials, components, and structures. This environment supports interdisciplinary collaboration and partnerships with academic and industrial institutions in Denmark and internationally. The candidate(s) will work within a research culture that combines computational development with physical experimentation and full scale construction.

SDU CREATE is a partner in CEBE, a ten-year national research initiative funded by the Villum Foundation, in which Danish technical universities collaborate to advance the sustainability of the built environment within planetary boundaries. Within this initiative, SDU CREATE leads research in Digitalisation and Automation, RF4, and contributes to research in Design for Regeneration, Circularity, and Longevity, RF2. The programme provides a long-term research framework, access to national research networks, and opportunities for collaboration with academic and industrial partners.

Responsibilities

The successful candidate(s) will contribute to the development and delivery of CREATE’s research activities and laboratory-based investigations. Responsibilities include:

  • Conducting high-quality research within the defined research project and contributing original, scientifically rigorous outcomes

  • Conducting fabrication experiments and biological and environmental performance testing, including operation of robotic systems and laboratory equipment as relevant to the candidate’s research profile

  • Participating in CREATE’s research team activities, contributing to the development of design, fabrication, and testing frameworks

  • Developing and maintaining computational tools and workflows supporting the research activities

  • Assisting in teaching bachelor’s and master’s level courses and workshops, including co-supervision of thesis students and collaboration with interns in research-related activities

  • Disseminating research results through high-impact peer-reviewed publications and recognised international conferences

  • Sharing research outcomes through curated and high-quality outputs for digital platforms, exhibitions, and competitions

  • Contributing to the further development and maintenance of CREATE’s laboratory infrastructures and experimental facilities

  • Engaging with academic and industrial collaborators at the national and international level, including participation in the Villum CEBE research network

  • Assisting senior staff in the preparation of applications for external research funding

Engagement in these activities will evolve with the experience of the candidate(s), contributing to the Centre’s excellence and supporting their academic development, ideally towards future career advancement.

Candidate Requirements

Applications are invited from highly motivated candidates holding a Master’s degree in architecture, computational design, civil or architectural engineering, materials science, environmental engineering, biology, or other relevant disciplines related to the research areas. Candidates must demonstrate primary expertise in either Bioreceptive Design and Robotic 3D Printing or Living Material Design and Biological Performance, and the ability to contribute to shared design, fabrication and validation activities. Interdisciplinary experience connecting these areas is particularly valued.

Candidates must demonstrate:

  • Documented interest and foundational knowledge in bioreceptive design, living system integration or related research areas

  • Competence in Grasshopper and Rhino, advanced for the Bioreceptive Design and Robotic 3D Printing profile and at working level for the Living Material Design and Biological Performance profile, together with relevant programming skills such as Python or C#

  • For the Bioreceptive Design and Robotic 3D Printing profile: practical experience in computational design, toolpath generation and robotic 3D printing, together with an understanding of biological requirements relevant to design; experience developing porous geometries and printable mineral materials are particularly valued

  • For the Living Material Design and Biological Performance profile: practical experience in material formulation and biological experimentation or cultivation, together with competence in experimental measurement and data analysis; experience with hydrogels, sensor integration, automated monitoring or hygrothermal characterisation are particularly valued

  • Hands-on laboratory experience, including physical prototyping or specimen preparation, and experimental testing relevant to the selected profile

  • Demonstrated capacity to conduct, document and disseminate projects and research outcomes suitable for peer-reviewed publication

  • Strong proficiency in English, both written and oral

  • Strong ability to work effectively within interdisciplinary teams and to coordinate and collaborate daily

  • Strong communication skills across graphical, written and oral formats

  • A proven track record of involvement in research or innovation projects; experience in teaching assistance, peer-reviewed publications or engagement with academic or industry stakeholders is evaluated positively

Contact information

For further information about the position(s) and SDU CREATE’s activities, please contact the Head of Centre, Associate Professor Roberto Naboni, at ron@iti.sdu.dk. For additional information on the Centre’s work, visit the website at www.create-sdu.com. 

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Find full information about how to apply as well as assessment and employment terms on our website!

title: Postdoc Position (2 years) in Manufacturing Technology & Industrial Management
description:
The Department of Technology and Innovation (ITI) at University of Southern Denmark (SDU), section of Engineering Operations Management, invites applications for a 2-year position as Postdoc in Manufacturing Technology & Industrial Management.  The position is open from December 1, 2026, and the job location is Odense, Denmark.

 

Job description  

Successful candidates will drive internationally competitive research, collaborate in and across disciplines, work closely with industry and attract competitive external research and innovation funding in collaboration with senior researchers. The candidates will play a key role in providing outstanding education, supervise students, and develop junior research staff. 

 

We offer 

We offer a vigorous international research environment with a balance of male and female researchers, excellent facilities, including the new Robotics and Additive Manufacturing Laboratories at University of Southern Denmark, a long-term strategic initiative created to support research, teaching, and industrial collaboration and experimentation. SDU expects to increase its’ collaboration with industrial companies and associations in the coming years. 

This position will imply collaboration with industrial partners in the Renewable Energy Sector. Examples can be vendors of wind turbines, electrification solutions, electrolyzers, biogas equipment, carbon capture, utilization and storage technologies etc. It can also be major owners / operators of renewable energy plants, as offshore wind turbine park operators, green hydrogen / methanol / ammonia plants etc.

Research will be done to support DK and EU in realizing ambitions for production of green energy at off-take prices competitive with energy from fossil fuels via scaling and industrialization, whether the energy is in the form of green electricity or green fuels for industry and transport. There will be specific emphasis on research into the interplay between business strategy, product design, manufacturing systems design, manufacturing technology choices and scenarios or plans for industrial scaling. In addition to that, the position offers the opportunity to shape our educational and research and innovation programs by contributing to teaching and supervision in areas of Manufacturing technologies of the future and Industrial Management to benefit from new developments in research fields, approaches and content.

Candidates must have a relevant PhD.

title: PhD Scholarship in Software for Sustainable Farming
description:
Imagine a world where food production is in harmony with natural processes, farmers nurture healthy soils, and biodiversity thrives. In contrast, current monoculture farming systems undermine this future. Can you see how Robotics and Digital Twins can open opportunities for autonomously operating agricultural robots? Are you passionate about making agriculture more sustainable? If you share our passion for technology and the difference it can make in meeting the UN’s Sustainable Development Goals, perhaps you are our new PhD student.

At the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute (MMMI), University of Southern Denmark in Odense, you will be part of the Robotic Intercropping (https://roboticintercropping.eu) team working to break new ground at the absolute forefront of what is possible in safe operation of autonomous agricultural vehicles. These are needed to enable better land use and management. This project promotes sustainable economic growth and higher levels of technological innovation. It will benefit society and create a safer and smarter world by providing decent work for all. Furthermore, autonomous robots will make current labor-intensive cultivation systems (e.g., strip-cropping, targeted mechanical weed control, etc.) profitable, contributing to increased biodiversity locally and reducing the need for insecticide use.

 

Responsibilities and qualifications

The PhD project is funded by a grant from the Novo Nordisk Foundation for the project Robotic Intercropping (https://roboticintercropping.eu). The project involves four research partners from Denmark and the Netherlands. Thus, this PhD project will be an integral part of a broader research team, consisting of collaborating partners with a common passion for autonomous agricultural robotics and new sustainable farming practices.

The PhD project will combine lightweight agricultural robots, manipulators for managing crop competition, and digital twins for modeling the working environment. If selected, your main focus will be.

  • Digital Twins (DT). Development of a sophisticated DT as a dynamic representation of the field, modeling crop growth, canopy architecture, and competition for light, water, and nutrients. Integrate advanced sensors (e.g., spectral, LiDAR) and simulation tools to guide robotic actions for yield optimization and enhanced biodiversity.

 

Team and role

You will: 

  • Be a core member of a team developing lightweight, modular robots and digital twins for scalable, precise interventions in complex intercropping environments.

  • Engage in interdisciplinary research integrating robotic systems and digital twins with multi-modal sensing and AI, aligned with agronomist-defined needs.

  • Participate in integration and field testing with Robotic Intercropping partners.

  • Design software architecture; integrate multi-modal data and models (e.g., crop competition, farm-level); implement “what-if” simulation; develop robust interfaces (e.g., ROS) for planning, navigation, and precision actions.

  • Collaborate with experts in plant science, robotics, statistics, and AI to bridge agroecology and robotic control.

At MMMI you will be a part of the Software Engineering unit. Expected outcomes include conference and journal publications, experimental validation, conference presentations, and teaching-assistant experience.

 

Appointment

Appointment as a PhD fellow is a 3-year salaried position, and the monthly gross salary incl. pension is 37.075 DKK. If you have relevant postgraduate experience, you may be placed on a higher salary step.

The positions are available from December 2026 or as soon as possible thereafter. 

 

We expect

Degree. A two-year master’s degree (120 ECTS) in Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Software Engineering, Computer Science, or an equivalent field (or a comparable degree at the same academic level).

Nice to have:

  • Specialization in digital twins and software engineering of control systems (PhD#3).

  • Experience with swarm robotic systems, manipulator design, cyber-physical systems, SIMULINK, and robotic software development.

  • Knowledge of mechanical design, control system theory, statistics, actuation, sensing, rapid prototyping, and manufacturing.

  • Experience with tools such as ROS, Gazebo/NVIDIA Isaac/Omniverse or CoppeliaSim for simulation, and data/cloud platforms.

title: PhD Position in Reversible Programming for Energy Efficient Cyber-Physical Systems (MSCA Doctoral Network E-CoRe, DC12)
description:
The SDU Drone Center, part of the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for a 3-year PhD position on reversible programming languages and their use for energy efficient cyber-physical systems. The position is doctoral candidate DC12, "Energy Efficiency in Cyber-Physical Systems", in the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network E-CoRe. The position is available from 1 January 2027, and the specific start date will be agreed upon with the successful candidate.

The application deadline is November 1, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST).

 

The position is funded by the European Union under the Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Networks programme, grant agreement no. 101120187. MSCA eligibility rules apply, see the section "What we expect" below. Read more about the network at https://e-core.nws.cs.unibo.it/.

 

What we offer

E-CoRe is a European doctoral network on reversible computing. Reversible computation discards no information and therefore avoids the fundamental energy lower bound of conventional computing. The network trains a cohort of doctoral candidates who will improve and popularise reversible languages, algorithms, and architectures for energy-intensive applications. As one of the E-CoRe doctoral candidates you join a cohort at partner universities across Europe, take part in joint training schools and network events, and spend secondments at partner institutions, currently planned at the University of Bologna and the University of Manchester.

The main supervisor is Professor Ulrik Pagh Schultz, whose research spans programming languages, software engineering, robotics, and drones. You will be co-supervised by researchers from the Software Engineering section, and you will collaborate closely with the reversible computing group at the University of Copenhagen, which is also an E-CoRe partner. The position connects to other ongoing projects at the Drone Center, including WildBotics (a newly started Marie Skłodowska-Curie doctoral network) and Robotic Intercropping, and to local companies such as Spaceline.

The position addresses a programming languages question with an applied setting: how do we write software in reversible programming languages for systems where energy matters, and how much energy does this save? The setting is low-energy computations for cyber-physical systems such as perching aerial robots and IoT devices. The work belongs to the E-CoRe work package on applications and builds on the languages and tools developed elsewhere in the network. Concretely, the work includes the following:

  • Implementing algorithms in reversible programming languages and extending these languages where the application domain requires new constructs or idioms.

  • Integrating the resulting software into simulated cyber-physical systems, such as perching drones and IoT sensing scenarios.

  • Estimating energy consumption through combined hardware-level and system-level analysis, using the modelling framework developed in the network.

  • Answering the central research question of the position: how do the energy savings from reversible computation correlate with the I/O characteristics of the system?

  • Publishing the results at international conferences and in journals in programming languages, software engineering, and cyber-physical systems.

The position may involve co-supervising related student projects. You are expected to participate in the Drone Center's project portfolio and outreach activities and in the training programme of the E-CoRe network.

 

What we expect

We expect you to hold an MSc in computer science, software engineering, or a closely related field, or to complete one before the start date. The core of the work is programming languages and software. You do not need experience with drones or embedded hardware, and you do not need prior knowledge of reversible computing. You should have experience with, and an interest in, some of the following:

  • Programming language design and implementation.

  • Functional or declarative programming, or other work with languages beyond the mainstream.

  • Software design and development in languages such as C, C++, Rust, Python, or Haskell.

  • Algorithms and their analysis.

  • Simulation, modelling, or energy estimation of computing systems.

  • Embedded, real-time, or robotic software.

We expect you to write and speak English fluently, to work independently and with an international team, and to travel for the secondments and network events described above. We furthermore expect you to publish findings at recognised international conferences and in peer-reviewed journals.

The position follows the rules of the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions, and you must meet all of the following conditions at the recruitment date:

  • You do not hold a doctoral degree. Applicants who have defended a doctoral thesis but not yet been awarded the degree are not eligible.

  • Mobility rule: you have not resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the recruitment date. Short stays such as holidays are disregarded, as is compulsory national service and time covered by the 1951 Refugee Convention.

  • You are eligible regardless of nationality.

Recruitment follows the European Charter for Researchers and the Code of Conduct for the Recruitment of Researchers. The process is open, transparent, merit-based, and equitable. The position is also announced on the Euraxess portal.

 

Workplace description

The SDU Drone Center is part of the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute at the Faculty of Engineering, located on the main SDU campus in Odense. At the center we research civilian drone technologies and their applications in agriculture, inspection, energy, healthcare, and nature conservation. We collaborate closely with companies in the robotics community around Odense and with research partners in Denmark and abroad. You will be part of an international group of PhD students, postdocs, engineers, and faculty working on autonomous systems and the software behind them.

 

Further information

For further information, please contact Professor Ulrik Pagh Schultz (ups@mmmi.sdu.dk).

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Before applying the candidates are advised to read the Faculty information for prospective PhD students and the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include:

  1. Motivated application.

  2. Curriculum Vitae.

  3. A statement of where you have resided and carried out your main activity in the 36 months before the expected recruitment date, to document the MSCA mobility rule.

  4. List of publications and maximum 2 examples of relevant publications (in case you have any publications).

  5. Master's and Bachelor's degree certificates or equivalent, including transcripts of grades (original and an official English translation).

  6. Completed TEK PhD application form for 5+3 applicants. Find the form at the Faculty website.

  7. Completed TEK PhD form for calculation grade point average. Find the form at the Faculty website.

  8. An official document describing the grading scheme of the awarding universities (if not Danish).

  9. Only for applicants from programmes that evaluate thesis/examination project by approved/not approved: An official written assessment of the thesis or dissertation project from the grade giving institution. The statement must clearly state that the candidate has been among the top 30 pct. in the graduation class for the study programme.

  10. References may be included, you're welcome to use the form for reference letter at the Faculty website.

  11. A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected.

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under 'Cover letter' (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under 'Resume' (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under 'Miscellaneous documents' (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file).

 

The application deadline is November 1, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST)

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU. Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation.

 

Enrollment and employment terms

Appointment as a PhD fellow is a 3-year salaried position. The position follows the MSCA Doctoral Networks funding rules. The MSCA contribution consists of a monthly living allowance of EUR 5,325.28, a monthly mobility allowance of EUR 710, and, where applicable, a monthly family allowance of EUR 660. These amounts are gross contributions to the employer. The salary paid to you is derived from these amounts after employer costs and is subject to Danish income tax and social contributions. If you have relevant postgraduate experience, this may be reflected in the salary placement within the Danish collective agreement.

The preferred start date is from 1 January 2027.

Applicants must hold a master's degree (equivalent to a Danish master's degree) at the time of enrollment and employment. Employment is contingent on enrollment approved by the PhD School. Enrollment will be in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order). Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for PhD fellows as described therein as well as the Protocol on PhD fellows signed by the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC).

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants' previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation.

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a "self-organizer".

 

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

title: PhD Position(s) in Computational Design and Robotic Fabrication for Timber Upcycling
description:
SDU CREATE invites highly motivated candidates who wish to contribute to a more sustainable built environment to apply for a PhD position in Computational Design and Robotic Fabrication for Timber Upcycling. The position(s) are expected to begin in January 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The application deadline is 15 October 2026 at 23:59 CEST.

 

Scope of the work

The PhD position(s) is linked to the Villum CEBE programme, Civil Engineering and the Green Transition in the Built Environment, funded by the Villum Foundation. Within Research Field 2, Design for Regeneration, Circularity and Longevity, the overall ambition is to extend the life cycle of reclaimed timber and retain its stored carbon for longer by transforming discarded wood into durable, materially efficient architectural components.

The research will investigate how heterogeneous pieces of waste timber can be reconstituted into engineered components with differentiated geometries and material properties. Computational design will connect architectural form, structural performance and available material stock, exploring how the arrangement, orientation and combination of reclaimed wood can generate new possibilities for building elements. The project will identify and develop suitable bonding techniques, integrate robotic fabrication with material characterisation, and demonstrate the resulting architectural systems at full scale.

We seek candidates with primary expertise in one of two complementary research profiles:

  • Computational Design and Robotic Fabrication: focusing on architectural design workflows, material allocation, robotic tooling, and the development of lamination, shaping and fabrication procedures for reclaimed timber.

  • AI-driven Computational Engineering: focusing on machine learning for material characterisation and property prediction, finite element modelling, structural optimisation, and experimental testing of timber, bonded interfaces and laminated components.

The successful candidate(s) will work within a team to develop and validate stock-informed design methods through computational investigation, hands-on fabrication experiments and full-scale architectural demonstrators. The candidate(s) will also contribute to the Centre’s activities, including teaching in the MSc CREATE programme and the BSc programme in Civil and Architectural Engineering through laboratory teaching, workshops, and co-supervision of student projects

 

Focus Area and Research Project

The research will develop new approaches to timber upcycling that minimise waste, extend carbon storage and advance circular construction. It will connect architectural design, material engineering and robotic fabrication to transform discarded timber into durable building components, developing lamination and bonding techniques alongside computational methods for design and structural optimisation.

The project builds on SDU CREATE’s previous research, including Re-VoxLam Truss and Re:Bridge, which explore how reclaimed timber can be reconstituted into structurally efficient architectural systems. Applicants are encouraged to consult the associated publications on reclaimed voxel lamination and stock and stress informed design and fabrication.

The successful candidate(s) will contribute to selected areas according to their expertise, working within a team with complementary skills:

  • Computational design and material allocation informed by available timber stock

  • Development of lamination and bonding techniques for architectural components

  • Robotic tooling and fabrication process development

  • Machine learning for material assessment and property prediction

  • Finite element modelling, structural optimisation and experimental validation

  • Fabrication and testing of full scale architectural demonstrators

  • Evaluation of material efficiency, structural performance and environmental benefits

 

About SDU CREATE’s Research Environment

The Centre for Computational Research in Emergent Architectural Technology and Engineering, SDU CREATE, is led by Associate Professor Roberto Naboni. The Centre investigates advanced concepts and applications in architectural engineering, focusing on computational design, construction robotics, and material innovation. SDU CREATE brings together an international research team working across architectural engineering, computer science, robotics, materials science, and biology. Its research develops sustainable, regenerative approaches to designing and constructing the built environment.

Located within the Faculty of Engineering at the University of Southern Denmark, SDU CREATE provides advanced laboratory facilities for robotic fabrication, additive and subtractive manufacturing, mixed reality applications in design and construction, and structural and mechanical testing. The facilities include industrial robotic systems, computational design platforms, and equipment for the experimental testing of materials, components, and structures. This environment supports interdisciplinary collaboration and partnerships with academic and industrial institutions in Denmark and internationally. The candidate(s) will work within a research culture that combines computational development with physical experimentation and full scale construction.

SDU CREATE is a partner in CEBE, a ten-year national research initiative funded by the Villum Foundation, in which Danish technical universities collaborate to advance the sustainability of the built environment within planetary boundaries. Within this initiative, SDU CREATE leads research in Digitalisation and Automation, RF4, and contributes to research in Design for Regeneration, Circularity, and Longevity, RF2. The programme provides a long-term research framework, access to national research networks, and opportunities for collaboration with academic and industrial partners.

 

Responsibilities

The successful candidate(s) will contribute to the development and delivery of CREATE’s research activities and laboratory-based investigations. Responsibilities include:

  • Conducting high-quality research within the defined research project and contributing original, scientifically rigorous outcomes

  • Conducting fabrication and structural testing experiments, including operation of robotic systems and laboratory equipment as relevant to the candidate’s research profile

  • Participating in CREATE’s research team activities, contributing to the development of design, fabrication, and testing frameworks

  • Developing and maintaining computational tools and workflows supporting the research activities

  • Assisting in teaching bachelor’s and master’s level courses and workshops, including co-supervision of thesis students and collaboration with interns in research-related activities

  • Disseminating research results through high-impact peer-reviewed publications and recognised international conferences

  • Sharing research outcomes through curated and high-quality outputs for digital platforms, exhibitions, and competitions

  • Contributing to the further development and maintenance of CREATE’s laboratory infrastructures and experimental facilities

  • Engaging with academic and industrial collaborators at the national and international level, including participation in the Villum CEBE research network

  • Assisting senior staff in the preparation of applications for external research funding

Engagement in these activities will evolve with the experience of the candidate(s), contributing to the Centre’s excellence and supporting their academic development, ideally towards future career advancement.

 

Candidate Requirements

Applications are invited from highly motivated candidates holding a Master’s degree in architecture, civil or architectural engineering, robotics, mechanical engineering, materials science, or other relevant disciplines related to the research areas. Candidates must demonstrate primary expertise in either Computational Design and Robotic Fabrication or AI-driven Computational Engineering, together with the ability to contribute to shared design, fabrication and validation activities.

Candidates must demonstrate:

  • Documented interest and foundational knowledge in circular construction, timber engineering or material upcycling

  • Competence in Grasshopper and Rhino, advanced for the Computational Design and Robotic Fabrication profile and at working level for the AI-driven Computational Engineering profile, together with relevant programming skills such as Python or C#

  • For the Computational Design and Robotic Fabrication profile: practical experience in robotic fabrication and development of computational design workflows; experience developing robotic tools, fixtures or fabrication procedures is particularly valued

  • For the AI-driven Computational Engineering profile: competence in finite element analysis and structural optimisation; practical experience developing and evaluating machine learning models is particularly valued

  • Hands-on laboratory experience with fabrication, including physical prototyping or specimen preparation, and experimental testing relevant to the selected profile

  • Demonstrated capacity to conduct, document, and disseminate projects and research outcomes suitable for peer-reviewed publication

  • Strong proficiency in English, both written and oral

  • Strong ability to work effectively within interdisciplinary teams and to coordinate and collaborate daily

  • Strong communication skills across graphical, written, and oral formats

  • A proven track record of involvement in research or innovation projects; experience in teaching assistance, peer-reviewed publications or engagement with academic or industry stakeholders is evaluated positively

 

Contact information

For further information about the position(s) and SDU CREATE’s activities, please contact the Head of Centre, Associate Professor Roberto Naboni, at ron@iti.sdu.dk. For additional information on the Centre’s work, visit www.create-sdu.com.

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Find full information on how to apply as well as assessment and employment terms on our website!

description:
.

Work tasks: Main Duties
• Prepare and cook a wide range of restaurant products, including savory and sweet dishes, baked products, pastries, dough products, fillings, sauces, soups, salads, desserts, and meat and fish dishes, according to established recipes and standards. • Prepare, roll, stretch, layer, fill, and handle dough and ensure consistent taste, texture, portioning, appearance, and presentation of finished products. • Organize and coordinate daily kitchen production, monitor product availability and workflow, adjust production when necessary, and maintain quality while minimizing waste. • Prepare and maintain the customer display/service line, including baking semi-ready products, arranging products, and ensuring appropriate availability, replenishment, presentation, and cleanliness. • Organize, coordinate, supervise, and control the daily operations of the restaurant-bakery, including customer service, kitchen and production activities, cleaning, storage, inventory, and overall operational readiness. • Prepare and coordinate daily, weekly, and monthly operational plans, including staffing, production, inventory, cleaning, maintenance, and other recurring requirements. • Monitor stock, ingredients, expiration dates, deliveries, inventory, write-offs, storage, and waste, and assist with ordering and stocktaking. • Maintain and ensure compliance with food safety, hygiene, cleaning, allergen management, occupational safety, equipment, and workplace requirements. • Guide, supervise, train, and support cooks and other assigned employees; provide instructions and feedback, assess their job performance, coordinate their work and priorities, and ensure assigned duties are properly and fully completed by assigned employees. • Communicate and coordinate effectively with servers, cleaners, management, suppliers, contractors, and other service providers to support smooth kitchen and restaurant operations. • Participate in and coordinate employee recruitment, including reviewing CVs and applications, communicating with candidates, conducting interviews, assessing candidates against position requirements, and supporting the selection of suitable employees. • Prepare and coordinate employee schedules, breaks, replacements, and staff deployment, adjusting staffing according to workload, absences, and operational requirements. • Monitor customer service and assist service staff when operationally necessary, particularly during busy periods, breaks, staff shortages, or absences. • Complete and monitor required production, inventory, cleaning, temperature, write-off, operational, and other records, checklists, documents, and reports. • Manage and participate in recipe implementation, menu and product development, testing, new-product introduction, and continuous improvement. • Identify operational or employee-performance deficiencies, take appropriate corrective action within assigned authority, and report significant issues to the Manager. • Take all appropriate actions and provide support the Manager in implementing operational decisions, procedures, standards, schedules, and plans and provide accurate information regarding restaurant operations. • Where specifically authorized and assigned in writing by the Employer, assume designated operational and supervisory responsibilities during the Manager’s absence.

We offer: - An opportunity to be part of a dynamic and innovative company with ambitious growth plans.
- A friendly and supportive professional international team with diverse experience that values each member’s contribution. - Modern working conditions and professional-grade equipment. - Competitive pay. - Career opportunities and personal development. - Affordable meals in our restaurant bakery.

Selle saavutamiseks peab klienditööjuht: - omama terviklikku ülevaadet kogu meie kliendibaasist; - toetama ja arendama tegevusjuhendajaid klienditöös; - juhendama tegevusjuhendajaid erinevates teemades, mh tegema individuaalseid vestluseid tegevusjuhendajatega; käima vajaduspõhiselt kaasas korteri koosolekutel; ettevalmistama juhendajat ja klienti SKAsse hindamistele minemisel; oskama soovitada kliendi juhendamiseks sobivaid metoodikaid, jne. - kasutama juhtumikorralduse põhimõtteid - märkama ja lahendama juhtumeid; - viima koos tegevusjuhendajaga läbi vajaduspõhiseid meeskonnatöid; - tegema koostööd juhtkonnaga; - tegema koostööd kvaliteedijuhiga; - korraldama tegevusjuhendajate asendused; - koordineerima päeva- ja tegevuskeskuste tegevusi, sh vaatama üle kuuplaanid; - integreerima alustavad tegevusjuhendajad tööellu; - koordineerima töötubade tööd; - juhendama praktikante.

Omalt poolt pakume: Pakume Sulle:
- toetavat kollektiivi; - regulaarseid juhtkonna kohtumisi väljakutsete arutamiseks; - avatud suhtlemisega ning arengule suunatud kolleege; - regulaarseid meeskonna infotunde; - juba toimivat meeskonda; - lisa puhkepäevad jõulude või aastavahetuse eel; - preemia tulemusliku töö eest. Meil on kokkuhoidev ja hea õhkkonnaga töökollektiiv. Sind ootab koostöövalmis juba toimiv meeskond, kus on avatud suhtlemine ning teineteisega arvestamine. Juhtkonna liikmena on Sul tagatud toetus teiste juhtkonna liikmete poolt. Me väärtustame arengut, mistõttu toimuvad regulaarselt koolitused ja õppereisid.

title: Lukksepp-keevitaja
description:
MIG/MAG keevitus -> rasketehnika /hüdrosilindrid

Tööülesanded: Sinu igapäevased kangelasteod:
Hüdrosilindri detailide keevitus: hülss/vars ja muud detailid. Kulbi terade vahetus: lõikus/keevitus. Detailide sirgestamine: (tõstuki kahvlid) kuumutamine/painutus/sirgestus. Rasketehnika masti ja detailide keevitus: mõrad- faasimine/keevitus. Ja palju muud... Meeskonna toetamine defekteerimisel ja masinate lahtivõtmisel. Töö on mitmekülgne ja eriprojekte on palju. Võimalus õppida juurde lihtsamat treitööd! Sellel teekonnal on toeks kogu meeskond, sest tihti hõlmab masina või hüdrosilindri remont mitut etappi: -Lahtivõtt ja defekteerimine -Pakkumise tegemine/eeldatavad töötunnid projektile -Tööde planeerimine -Võimalikud treitööd -Materjalide tellimine -Keevitus/kooste -Avade taastamine -Sirgestus -Uute detailide valmistamine /tellimine -Joonestamine -Hooldus -Montaaž See on ülevaade kogu meeskonna tööst! Kui oled meeskonnamängija, siis see üldsegi mitte igav ja mitmekülgne töö võib olla just Sulle! Me ei eelda, et Sa oskad kõike. Kui Sul on suur huvi rasketehnika ja metallitööde vastu, siis see on juba kõige olulisem. Kuulutuses märgitud palk ei ole ülempiir- see on meie miinimum. Initsiatiiv+motivatsioon+tööde teostamise kiirus= kõrgem palk! Kui soovid täpsemat tööde kirjeldust, siis helista või tule kohale meiega tutvuma!

Omalt poolt pakume: Meie poolt on Sulle tasuta lõuna.
Maksame isikliku sõiduauto kompensatsiooni. Palk kuni 3500 € bruto. Kui planeerid ja teed oma tööd eriti hästi ja efektiivselt, tulevad mängu boonused – ehk siis 3500 € ei ole lagi! Hästi varustatud töökoda ja toetav tiim, kes hindab head nalja sama kõrgelt kui kvaliteetselt remonditud tehnikat.

Muud nõuded: Mida me Sinult ootame
Põhioskused: MIG/MAG keevitus. Oled eelisjärjekorras kui: Sul on varasem reaalne kokkupuude rasketehnika hooldusega, teadmised hüdraulikast, hüdrosilindritest ning tunned metalli ja selle töötlemist. Kuldne tase: kui oskad vahetada hüdrosilindril tihendid täiesti iseseisvalt ja seda ka testida/stendida (220bar). Oled meil kohe nimekirja tipus! Lisapunktid: TIG keevitus ja elektrood ning oskus teha lihtsamaid treitöid manuaalsel treipingil annavad sulle tugeva eelise. Võidab siiski kirg rasketehnika vastu ja soov/tahe töötada metalliga!

title: Tugiisik
description:
Tööülesanded: Kas tunned, et soovid teha tööd, millel on päriselt tähendus? Kas lastega suhtlemine toob sulle rõõmu ning soovid olla kellelegi toeks tema igapäevases kasvamises ja arengus?
Meie meeskond ootab endaga liituma tugiisikut, kes soovib panustada laste heaolusse, turvatundesse ja enesekindluse kasvamisse. Sinu roll tugiisikuna: olla lapsele igapäevane toetaja ja julgustaja; aidata kaasa lapse arengule ja iseseisvuse kujunemisele; luua turvaline ja hooliv keskkond; teha koostööd pere ja spetsialistidega. See ei ole lihtsalt töö – see on võimalus olla kellelegi oluline tugi ja turvatunne.

Omalt poolt pakume: Püsivat tööd;
Toetavat meeskonda ja sisekoolitusi; Tähendusrikast ja südantsoojendavat tööd; Toetavat meeskonda ja juhendamist; Võimalust päriselt midagi muuta ühe lapse elus.

Muud nõuded: Otsime tugiisikuid, kes sobivad hästi lastega, on kohusetundlikud ja peavad kinni kokkulepetest ning on soovitavalt läbinud tugiisiku koolituse või valmis seda läbima.
Ootame sind, kui: hoolid lastest ja soovid nendega töötada; oled kannatlik, empaatiline ja usaldusväärne; suudad märgata lapse vajadusi ja pakkuda tuge; oled valmis õppima ja arenema.

Omalt poolt pakume: • 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗶𝗹𝘀𝘂𝘀𝘁: Kindlat ja pikaajalist tööd elutähtsas valdkonnas.

Tööülesanded: CareMate otsib oma meeskonda tugiisikuid, kes soovivad toetada täisealisi inimesi iseseisvama igapäevaelu saavutamisel ja säilitamisel.

Tugiisiku roll on inimest juhendada ja võimestada, mitte teha igapäevaseid tegevusi tema eest ära. Töö ei sisalda hooldustoimingute tegemist.

Omalt poolt pakume: CareMate pakub:
Paindlikku töökoormust ja tööaega; Võimalust valida endale sobiv teeninduspiirkond Tallinnas; Võimalust enne koostöö alustamist teenuse kasutajaga kohtuda; Koordinaatori tuge ja vajalikku juhendamist; digitaalseid töövahendeid; Nädalavahetustel kõrgemat tasu; Tähenduslikku ja vastutusrikast tööd.

Muud nõuded: Sobid tugiisikuks, kui sul on vähemalt üks järgnevatest: läbitud tugiisiku väljaõpe; läbitud tegevusjuhendaja väljaõpe või sissejuhatav koolitus; tegevusjuhendaja kutse või vastav kutseharidus; erialane kutse- või kõrgharidus sotsiaaltöö, sotsiaalpedagoogika, eripedagoogika, tegevusteraapia, psühholoogia, vaimse tervise õenduse või alushariduse pedagoogika valdkonnas.
Ootame, et oled: usaldusväärne, empaatiline ja hea suhtleja; oskad inimest rahulikult juhendada ja motiveerida; valmis töötama iseseisvalt ning tegema koostööd tugivõrgustikuga; vajalike digioskustega; valmis oma tööd lühidalt dokumenteerima.

title: IT Service Manager to an international energy company, Espoo
description:
About the role

In this role, you will work at the intersection of business operations and IT, taking end-to-end ownership of a portfolio of digital services and applications supporting large-scale hydropower operations. You will act as a crucial link between business stakeholders, architects, internal delivery teams, and external suppliers, ensuring that IT services remain secure, cost-efficient, reliable, and continuously evolving.

This is a 12-month fixed-term contract with a strong possibility of extension. The position offers a flexible hybrid work model (2–3 days a week at the office) and is based in Espoo. Occasional travel within the Nordic countries is expected.

We offer:
- High-impact ownership: Direct end-to-end responsibility for digital services supporting critical hydropower infrastructure
- Professional growth: A supportive, expert community where you are trusted to challenge yourself and develop your skills
- Hybrid work model: Flexibility to combine remote work with office presence (2–3 days a week at Espoo office)

Work tasks
- Own the end-to-end lifecycle of a portfolio of Hydro IT services and applications
- Act as a trusted advisor to business stakeholders, translating operational needs into clear service roadmaps and action plans
- Drive service performance, availability, cybersecurity, compliance, and user experience
- Lead supplier collaboration, overseeing service quality, vendor commitments, contracts, and costs
- Prioritize development initiatives in close alignment with business owners, architects, and delivery teams
- Ensure all services align with internal IT service management standards, architecture principles, and continuity requirements

We are looking for

- A relevant academic background (Bachelors or Masters degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Software Engineering, or a related field)
- Solid experience in IT service management, application management, or digital service delivery
- Good understanding of ITIL practices, agile development, and the lifecycle of business-critical applications
- Practical experience in supplier management, service governance, and cost tracking/budgeting
- Proactive, structured, and self-driven mindset with the confidence to take ownership of complex entities
- Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills
- Full fluency in English (written and spoken)

It is considered a strong advantage if you have:
- Experience within the energy sector, operational technology (OT), or industrial digitalization
- Proficiency in Finnish or Swedish

Our recruitment process

This recruitment process is handled by Academic Work and it is our clients wish that all questions regarding the position is directed to Academic Work.

Our selection process is continuous and the advert may close before the recruitment process is completed if we have moved forward to the next phase. The process includes two tests: one personality test and one cognitive test. The tests are tools to find the right talent for the right position, to enable equality, diversity, and a fair process.

title: HR Systems & Integration Specialist, Helsinki
description:
